entries.reason: Metal 4's queue label is READONLY - MTL4CommandQueue.h:218 declares `@property (readonly, nullable) NSString* label`, and atomic is the default a property has - so the port answers the value and does not offer a setter, and the value arrives the way Metal 4 says it does, through the descriptor: -[MTLDevice newMTL4CommandQueueWithDescriptor:error:] takes descriptor.label and nothing else of the descriptor, because this queue has no feedback queue to report to. A fresh queue answers nil. The one place that sets it is -[RevenantMetal4CommandQueue revenantSetLabel:], the port's own seam, and THAT has no registry row: carried_api() excludes a toolchain* name because the port's own classes are its machinery and it does not name them, so a row for it could never be answered by any build - measured 2026-10-04, where the 6.1.3 gate on land-w19 answered "listed as implemented, but nothing of that name is built: -[RevenantMetal4CommandQueue revenantSetLabel:]"

entries.reason: Every resource of this port is CPU-resident whatever the application asked for - a buffer is its own bytes and a texture is read and written on the CPU - so the residency a set would make is already the case and the residency it would remove is not there to remove (facts/Metal/Blits.md, "The access hints", and facts/Metal/Heaps.md, "Hazard tracking and storage modes"). This is the same shape as -[MTLCommandBuffer optimizeContentsForCPUAccess:] in that file: doing nothing, because what the call asks for is already so, and NO member of this group prints a line - a caller that added a set and heard a refusal would be told its resources are not resident, which on this port is false

entries.reason: A drawable of this port is a texture already drawn into the EAGL framebuffer, and a draw is a call into OpenGL ES 2.0 that has already been made by the time it is encoded - the fact facts/Metal/Heaps.md gives for hazard tracking, where there is nothing to track for the same reason. So the display is never holding a drawable this queue still needs back, and rendering to one is complete when the encoding returns. -waitForDrawable:'s own header says it "returns immediately and doesn't perform any synchronization on the current thread", which is what this body is, and -signalDrawable: schedules a signal for a completion that has already happened; neither triggers the presentation, which is -[MTLCommandQueue presentDrawable:]'s own work and the application's to ask for. NO member of this pair prints a line, and no check reaches them
entries.effect: ONLY THE PLACEMENT IS VERIFIED, and it says why: a drawable of this port cannot be made without a device, and the emulated guest has no EAGL context to make one ("an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 2.0 on this guest: NIL", with the run's emulator.log naming the renderer "Revenant GLES 1.1 Vulkan (SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0))"), so no case on that guest reaches it; the host cannot either, because this file needs OpenGLES/EAGL.h and that is a DEVICE framework. What the row claims is the placement and the reason, and a device run asks it when one is attached.. The method is on the queue: `nm` on the probe binary of 2026-10-04 carries -[RevenantMetal4CommandQueue waitForDrawable:] and, before the placement fix, the same selector only on -[RevenantMetalDevice(RevenantMetal4CommandQueue26) waitForDrawable:] - all fourteen members of this protocol were answering on the device and on no queue, which is what the corpus recorded as `missing` for every one of them (coordination/corpus/ledger-2026-10-03/Metal.tsv).

entries.reason: Done natively over the port's own event. RevenantMetalSharedEvent carries a state of its own - a signalled value, a setter for it, and a wait that blocks until the value is reached (Metal/MTLSharedEvent12.m) - and @protocol MTLSharedEvent is declared as a refinement of MTLEvent in the 26.2 SDK (MTLEvent.h:52), so the port's own event is an MTLEvent by shape. A GPU event is signalled when the work before it is complete, and on this backend that work is complete by the time the call is encoded, so the value is set now rather than scheduled; a wait blocks on the same value the port's own -[MTLSharedEvent waitUntilSignaledValue:timeout:] waits on. An event that is not one of the port's has no state to read or set, and THAT is refused by name: a value set on an object whose owner would never see it is worse than saying so
entries.effect: CHECKED ON THE GUEST by the device probe on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 10B329 of 2026-10-04: "ok   MTL4CommandQueue_waitForEvent: -waitForEvent:value: returns at once for a value the port's event has reached". The case waits for the value the signal in the case before it has just set, so it cannot block; a wait for a value nothing will signal is what the port's own -[MTLSharedEvent waitUntilSignaledValue:timeout:] is for and is not what this case is.. The method is on the queue: `nm` on the probe binary of 2026-10-04 carries -[RevenantMetal4CommandQueue waitForEvent:value:] and, before the placement fix, the same selector only on -[RevenantMetalDevice(RevenantMetal4CommandQueue26) waitForEvent:value:] - all fourteen members of this protocol were answering on the device and on no queue, which is what the corpus recorded as `missing` for every one of them (coordination/corpus/ledger-2026-10-03/Metal.tsv).. MTL4CommandQueue.h:274 and :308 spell the event `id<MTLEvent>` and this file spells it `id`, because iOS 6 has no MTLEvent to name and the SDK annotates the type 12.0 and later; the selector is the header's either way.

entries.reason: Done natively over the port's own event. RevenantMetalSharedEvent carries a state of its own - a signalled value, a setter for it, and a wait that blocks until the value is reached (Metal/MTLSharedEvent12.m) - and @protocol MTLSharedEvent is declared as a refinement of MTLEvent in the 26.2 SDK (MTLEvent.h:52), so the port's own event is an MTLEvent by shape. A GPU event is signalled when the work before it is complete, and on this backend that work is complete by the time the call is encoded, so the value is set now rather than scheduled; a wait blocks on the same value the port's own -[MTLSharedEvent waitUntilSignaledValue:timeout:] waits on. An event that is not one of the port's has no state to read or set, and THAT is refused by name: a value set on an object whose owner would never see it is worse than saying so

entries.reason: A drawable of this port is a texture already drawn into the EAGL framebuffer, and a draw is a call into OpenGL ES 2.0 that has already been made by the time it is encoded - the fact facts/Metal/Heaps.md gives for hazard tracking, where there is nothing to track for the same reason. So the display is never holding a drawable this queue still needs back, and rendering to one is complete when the encoding returns. -waitForDrawable:'s own header says it "returns immediately and doesn't perform any synchronization on the current thread", which is what this body is, and -signalDrawable: schedules a signal for a completion that has already happened; neither triggers the presentation, which is -[MTLCommandQueue presentDrawable:]'s own work and the application's to ask for. NO member of this pair prints a line, and no check reaches them
